concerns.text: FR-004 specifies a baseline *TinyLSTM (quantized transformer)*, but the Idea document later describes the baseline as a *quantized TinyBERT transformer*. TinyLSTM is not a transformer architecture, and TinyBERT is a transformer but exceeds the declared model‑size constraints. This inconsistency invalidates the core scientific claim of comparing a brain‑inspired model to a *standard transformer* baseline.

concerns.location: User Story 3 – Acceptance Scenario 2 (RSA permutation test convergence definition)
concerns.text: The permutation test uses an early‑stopping rule based on p‑value variance < 0.001 over the last 1,000 permutations. Early stopping biases the null distribution and can produce anti‑conservative p‑values unless a rigorously validated sequential Monte‑Carlo correction is applied. Recommend fixing the permutation count (e.g., always 10,000) or using a proper sequential testing framework.

The plan provides no formal power justification for the RSA comparison across three ROIs. There is no effect‑size estimate, Monte‑Carlo simulation, or reference to prior work that would ensure ≥ 80 % power. Without this, the study may be under‑powered to detect the hypothesised difference.

concerns.location: User Story 3 – Acceptance Scenario 1 (RSA computation description)
concerns.text: Inter‑subject variability is not addressed. RSA is described as being computed on BOLD signals averaged per story event, but it is unclear whether RSA matrices are computed per subject and then aggregated, or whether a subject‑level permutation is performed. Ignoring subject differences can confound model effects with individual variability.

concerns.location: User Story 3 – Acceptance Scenario 1 (RSA similarity metric)
concerns.text: RSA similarity is computed with Pearson correlation. Pearson assumes linear relationships and is sensitive to outliers; the RSA literature commonly uses rank‑based (Spearman/Kendall) or distance‑based metrics. The choice needs explicit justification or an alternative metric should be provided.
